native_mechanisms: Nightingales always land first on the unlocked stone carrying the smallest owed letter (greedy min-key selection over the frontier, with a landing justified by 'nothing cheaper can reach it now').
Threads cast from a tower price each road by its thief's directional toll (per-direction outgoing-edge relaxation: dist(u) + w(u,v) rebuilds the far stone's letter in place).
A locked letter is never rebuilt again, and threads reaching nowhere are dropped so their stones keep an unreadable debt forever (settled nodes are final; unreachable nodes stay at infinity).
A knot of three threads already cast at a stone can be detached and recast with a lower number, changing which stone the bird visits next (decrease-key on an already-queued node, in place).
core_technique: Dijkstra on a CSR graph with a linear-scanned (SIMD/AVX2) frontier array instead of a heap, batch-settling every frontier node whose tentative distance is <= max(min key, min over frontier of key + node's cheapest outgoing weight) — i.e. Crauser's OUT-criterion lookahead — with in-place decrease-key, and a binary-heap Dijkstra kept as a work-budget bail-out fallback.
